findings.title: The sign window's register reader takes only tag 121, so a site's valid Seedelf payment spelled in constructor 0's general form (tag 102) reads 'without a register: anyone can take' and 'Your private balance isn't in it'
findings.scenario: A connected site asks the public account to sign a transaction that pays 50 ₳ to Seedelf Wallet's contract under a valid, payable register (g, u). The register can be anyone's or the user's own Seedelf. The output's inline datum is written as d8 66 82 00 9f 58 30 <g> 58 30 <u> ff, which is 102([0, [_ g, u]]), the general form of Constr 0 [g, u]. The node accepts this spelling and decodes it as Constr 0 [g, u] (r3a#1's verifier ran cardano-cli on exactly this form). The deployed wallet.ak (5b82530) checks `if register is Register` on the decoded Data, so only the key for (g, u) can spend the output. The wallet's own readers take this spelling as a register: chain.ts registerOf and seedelf-koios register_of_datum both accept tag 102. If the register is the user's own, the 50 ₳ lands in their private balance and can be spent there. The sign window reads the output with a third copy, cip30's register_datum, which takes tag 121 only. So the window gets `seedelf: "none"` and shows dappUi.warn.noRegister: "It pays Seedelf Wallet's contract without a register: whatever goes there, anyone can take." That is false. The window should show dappUi.privacy.paysSeedelfAccount instead. signingTies also gets seedelf=false, so with no other ties its privacy line says "Your private balance isn't in it." That is false when the register is the user's own: the payment then links the public account to the private balance. A session's window says "Your public account and your private balance aren't in it." in the same case. Transaction details read the raw datum through the same function, so they show no register for this output. They also show none for 48-byte points written as chunked byte strings (W2's note). No money moves differently from what was signed. The user is told the wrong thing about who can spend the output and about what signing ties.
findings.since: fe8b7748 (2026-09-24, chunk 15) wrote register_datum for tag 121 only. register_of_datum learned tag 102 in 01f89534 (2026-09-26, launch review H4), and this copy wasn't updated with it. It is in every tagged release from web-wallet/1.6.0 on, and unchanged at web-wallet/1.9.1 (git diff web-wallet/1.9.1 HEAD shows nothing for cip30.rs).
findings.evidence:
1. wasm/src/cip30.rs:1007-1030 register_datum: `if d.tag()? != minicbor::data::Tag::new(121) { return Err(..."not constructor 0") }` (1011-1013), then `d.bytes()?` for both points (1015-1016). It has no 102 branch and reads definite bytes only. cip30.rs:999-1001: `fn is_register_datum(datum_hex) -> bool { register_datum(datum_hex).is_some_and(|r| build::is_payable(&r)) }`.
2. The window reads a re-encoded datum. cip30.rs:1150 decodes the site's transaction with `conway::Tx::decode_fragment` (not Minted). output_parts (cip30.rs:971-996) does `Some(conway::PseudoDatumOption::Data(d)) => { let bytes = d.0.encode_fragment()...` (981-983). In pallas-primitives-0.35.1 plutus_data.rs, decode at 332-338 reads tag 102 into `Constr { tag: 102, any_constructor: Some(..), fields }`, and encode at 360-364 writes tag 102 back with `(any_constructor, fields)`. So the 102 spelling reaches register_datum unchanged and is refused. BoundedBytes re-encode as definite at 48 bytes, which is why chunked points read as a register here but not in decode.rs.
3. cip30.rs:1385-1393: `Address::Shelley(s) if *s.payment().as_hash() == contract_hash => Some(if inline.as_deref().is_some_and(is_register_datum) {"register"} else {"none"} ...)`.
4. The UI: DappApprovals.tsx:1185-1189 shows `dapp-seedelf-unsafe` with dappUi.warn.noRegister (en.json:517) for "none". 1190-1194 shows paysSeedelfAccount (en.json:467) only for "register". 1316-1320 calls `signingTies(..., s.paid.some((p) => p.seedelf === "register"))`. ui/dapp.ts:128-137 adds `checked && !seedelf && t("dappUi.privacy.notPrivate")` (en.json:461, "Your private balance isn't in it.") on the public side, and `notAccountNorPrivate` for a session.
5. The other copies take the form. seedelf-koios/src/koios.rs:361-371 register_of_datum: `121 => {}`, `102 => { if d.array().ok()? != Some(2) || d.u64().ok()? != 0 { return None; } }`. extension/src/background/chain.ts:89-100 registerOf: `if (tag.arg === CONSTR_ANY) { ...pair.arg !== 2 ... index.arg !== 0 }`. Both are pinned with 102 in seedelf-koios/tests/rows_test.rs:133 and extension/tests/chain.test.ts:37. balances.ts:489-505 ownedUtxos (chain.ts registerOf, then wasm isOwned) and wasm lib.rs:2316 check_spendable (register_of_datum) both read the landed UTxO as the wallet's.
6. Transaction details: decode.rs:1222-1229 register_detail calls cip30's register_datum. decode.rs:1255 passes `d.0.raw_cbor()` (Minted output, bytes as written), and 1282-1285 show `register` only from it.
7. The contract: `git show 5b82530:seedelf-contracts/validators/wallet.ak` has `spend(maybe_register: Option<Data>, ...)` and `if register is Register { schnorr.prove(...) and list.has(extra_signatories, proof.vkh) } else { True }`. That is a Data-level check, so the spelling doesn't matter.
8. No test covers it. wasm/tests/cip30_test.rs:1374-1394 a_payment_into_seedelf_says_whether_it_has_a_register uses only REGISTER_DATUM (d8799f…, tag 121).
9. It contradicts E3b's checked line (E3b.md:151: 'never says the private balance isn't in it when a Seedelf is paid'). That holds only for the tag-121 spelling.
Nothing was run: traced from source.
findings.fix: Read the datum in register_datum with seedelf_koios::koios::register_of_datum. That reader takes tag 121 and 102([0, fields]), definite or indefinite fields, whole or chunked 48-byte points, and nothing after. The sign window, Transaction details and the wallet's own scan would then share one Rust reader. Fix the class, not this one copy. The other members are chain.ts registerOf (the worker's copy, which ownedUtxos and contract-scan call first), koios.rs register_of_datum, and core lovejoin parse_mix_datum (r3a#1). Both register readers also still refuse the indefinite pair 102([_ 0, fields]), which the node accepts (r3a#1's verifier). Hold the Rust reader and chain.ts to one shared vector file, as lovejoin-pool-vectors.json holds the depth walk's copies. It should list 121, 102 with a definite and an indefinite pair, indefinite fields and chunked bytes. d1#3 is the same label on register-shaped datums that can't be spent. Splitting the label three ways (payable register / register no one can spend / no register) fixes both. Test for the verifier: in cip30_test.rs, add `out(&contract, 2_000_000, Some(&format!("d86682009f5830{g}5830{u}ff")))` with g and u from REGISTER_DATUM. Expect paid[0].seedelf == Some("register"); today it is Some("none").
findings.owner_why: The fix changes only what the window says about an output, to match the wallet's own reader and the contract. It adds no refusal and changes no default.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md, docs/archive/plans/*.md, docs/plans/*.md, flows.md, architecture.md and privacy.md for 'general form', 'tag 102', '102([', '102 form', 'register_datum', 'is_register_datum', 'noRegister' and 'without a register'. The only hits: chunk-15 (the label's design), chunk-17:297 (the tree view reads tag 102), chunk-34:621 (pool datums) and flows.md:79 (ADA Handles). In the lanes: W2.md:188 covers chunked points in decode.rs only, d1#3 covers unpayable points, and r3a#1 with its verify covers parse_mix_datum and register_of_datum's indefinite pair. None covers tag 102 in cip30. It is not on SECURITY.md's out-of-scope list: a site writes the bytes, and no data source is involved.

guards.stops: is_payable: paying a register whose public value is the identity (anyone can take) or whose points are off the subgroup (locked). Used by the sign window's is_register_datum too

register_of_datum: anything but an exact Constr 0 of two 48-byte strings read as a register, token by token so a deep datum can't trap. Every Rust spend path reads registers through it (extract_bytes_with_logging)
registerOf: the worker's copy of the same rule, used by ownedUtxos and contract-scan's locator before WebAssembly's ownership check
within_depth: a datum nested past 128 levels reaching Pallas or uplc and trapping WebAssembly. Its TS copy is lovejoin.ts:2722 withinDepth

checked_ok: The depth walk: TS withinDepth (lovejoin.ts:2722) and core cbor::walk (cbor.rs:69) agree item for item. Both read heads of any width, treat reserved info 28-30 and an indefinite int or tag as invalid, check text as UTF-8 per chunk (minicbor 0.25.1's skip uses str_iter), take chunked strings only in the same major type, double a map's count with an overflow refusal, count a tag as one level, accept a break only for an indefinite container, check depth before an empty container, and refuse trailing bytes. Held by lovejoin-pool-vectors.json.

Register readers: chain.ts registerOf and koios register_of_datum accept the same spellings. Both take 121, or 102 with a definite pair and index 0; definite or indefinite fields; whole or chunked 48-byte points; and nothing after. Both refuse the same: other constructors, an indefinite 102 pair, wrong lengths. contract-scan's seedelfRow writes the register back canonically, which every reader takes.

TS evaluable matches core refusal/unreadable_datum: a reference script is refused, non-hex datum bytes read as no datum, and anything else goes through the depth walk. TS measurable matches core reference_script_size on Koios's shapes. private-index utxoOf turns a row's script flag into a script of unknown size, which both refuse.

Seedelf token tests: TS seedelfTokenOf (prefix 5eed0e1f) and wasm check_spendable's contains_policy_id (any token of the policy) agree. The deployed policy (5b82530 seedelf.ak with token_name.generate) mints only names that start with the prefix.

Network ids: the three wasm network_flag copies (cip30.rs:73, lovejoin.rs:61, lib.rs:2070) agree. wasm Network is Preprod=0 and Mainnet=1, and getNetworkId answers 0 and 1. networks.ts SHELLEY (preprod epoch 4 at 1,655,769,600,000; mainnet epoch 208 at 1,596,059,091,000) gives eval.rs slot_config's first slots, 86,400 and 4,492,800.

Lovejoin values: the classic 10 ₳ in all five TS copies = pool.rs CLASSIC_LOVELACE. The UI's MAX_BOXES, MAX_BOOTSTRAP_BOXES and MAX_TOKEN_BOOTSTRAP_BOXES = the worker's MAX_MIX_BOXES, MAX_DEPOSIT_BOXES and MAX_TOKEN_DEPOSIT_BOXES, with the same classic/other split (the UI's classic pool has no id, and the worker's mostBootstrap compares with CLASSIC). The pool floor is read from NETWORKS[network].lovejoin.poolFloor in every worker copy. The UI's '/pool has \d+ boxes/' matches core PoolShort's Display.

Fee estimate copies: the UI's MIX_FEE_ESTIMATE (0.95 ₳) and MIX_FEE_ESTIMATE_FOUR (1.35 ₳) and Lovejoin.tsx's DEPOSIT_RESERVE and BOOTSTRAP_BACK_LEAST (1.5 ₳) equal core's. COLLATERAL_MIX_COST (0.25 + 0.95 + 0.3 ₳) = COLLATERAL_TAIL_RESERVE. The UI's estimate leaves out INLINE_SCRIPTS_ESTIMATE, which never shows: a shown pool must have scriptsInline 0 (lovejoin-pools.ts verified()), and the classic pool's inline_scripts is empty. All of these are display only; what's funded comes from core through WebAssembly.

Error text matched across the boundary matches today's Rust: PUBLIC_SHORT, PRIVATE_SHORT, TOO_MANY, TOO_LARGE, TOO_LITTLE, NOT_ENOUGH_PRIVATE, NO_PRIVATE_PAYS, NOT_BECH32, the pool-has regex and dapp.ts's two prefixes ('The wallet can't read', 'bad request'). js_error passes the whole cause chain ({e:#}), and every api binding uses it (96 sites). TOO_LITTLE's 'insufficient lovelace' and 'Not Enough Lovelace' come only from external_sweep, which is the sweep return's builder.

Own-address rules: wasm is_own_address and the worker's ties/fartherKeys cover the same keys, 0-499 on each chain and only under an account's stake key past the first 20. activity.ts accountMatcher and account.ts count by payment key, as is_own_address does. cip30 own_address also requires the account's stake key, on purpose, for what a site's transaction returns. activity's someoneElse regex /^addr(_test)?1[zx2w]/ picks exactly the four script-payment header types. sessions.ts paysAccount's header test (even type 0-7) picks the key-payment types.

Collateral rules for the cancel and the chain: wasm fits_collateral = sessions.ts collateralFits. The chain's collateral is the worker's pick by OutRef (holdings_of). orders.rs cancel_orders needs ADA alone with no datum, which cancelOf's collateralFits/plainAda pick meets.

Histories: wasm merged_class and TS merged give the same sorted ids and origin ranks for what the worker sends, since activity.ts reads every class through readClass, which canonicalises the legacy 'public'.

Preference defaults: every worker read falls back to DEFAULT_PREFERENCES. account.ts's `?? false` applies only without a PreferencesService, and sw.ts always passes one (spends, line 205). The UI starts from DEFAULT_PREFERENCES (ui/preferences.tsx:28,34).

The Lovejoin stepper's copy of WebAssembly's public pick (Lovejoin.tsx publicPick and accountLeast) agrees with chain_from_account_at: the most of the token first, ADA-only UTxOs after, minimum_address_payment chunked 20 tokens to an output, and the 68-byte head of a 57-byte base address's output. Where the two differ, the copy errs low: on equal token quantities it takes the UTxO with less ADA first.
notes: r3a#1's family, a new fact: the worker's chain.ts registerOf shares register_of_datum's refusal of the indefinite pair 102([_ 0, fields]) (chain.ts:94, `pair.arg !== 2`). balances.ts ownedUtxos and contract-scan's locatorOf call chain.ts before WebAssembly does, so fixing koios.rs alone wouldn't make such a payment show. Unlike the depth walk, no shared vector holds the two register readers together. Each has its own tag-102 test (rows_test.rs:133, chain.test.ts:37). cip30's register_datum (x3#1) is a third copy, and the strictest.

e3a#2 and e8b#1's class, every copy: the collateral predicate exists in seven places. coin-control.ts isCollateralShaped (5 ₳, no tokens, any datum or script) and dapp.ts sessionCollateral (the same) are the loose two those findings name. sessions.ts collateralFits = wasm lovejoin.rs fits_collateral (strict). wasm lib.rs session_collateral: ADA alone and evaluable, so a datum is allowed; exactly 5 ₳ first, else the largest ≥ 2 ₳. core account_collateral and with_account: ADA alone. orders.rs cancel_orders: ADA alone, no datum. E2b's note on spareOf (sessions.ts:6400, which counts datum-bearing ADA-only UTxOs) is the same split. I found no money effect: collateralWanted subtracts the 5 ₳ once, and the return takes those UTxOs. One predicate per side, with a test holding collateralFits to fits_collateral, would fix the class.
E3b's checked line (E3b.md:151, signingTies never says the private balance isn't in it when a Seedelf is paid) holds only when the datum is spelled with tag 121: see x3#1.

Known, not re-reported: every Seedelf minimum (wallet_minimum_lovelace_with_assets, seedelf_minimum_lovelace) is sized against dummy_base_address, about 0.12 ₳ over the contract's enterprise address. chunk-34-token-pools.md:295 and :532 record it.

Hardcoded protocol parameters in TypeScript copies: Lovejoin.tsx:371 LEAST_PER_BYTE 4,310 (the stepper's accountLeast) and FEE_ROOM's 1.46 ₳ change least (Lovejoin.tsx:207-214); Staking.tsx:91 KEY_DEPOSIT 2 ₳ (E7b's note). If coinsPerUTxOByte moves, only the stepper and the pre-checks drift: the stepper could stop a box low or offer one the build refuses in words. No money moves on them.

lib.rs:1331 built_or_without_strangers labels a failure 'size' or 'cost' with `e.to_string().contains("over the network's limit")`, the outer message only. That is safe today, since no path wraps TooLarge in a context. A future .context() would turn 'size' into 'cost', a left-out reason label; build::is_too_large is the typed check.

Core's STAKE_SHORT (build.rs:488), ACCOUNT_LAUNCH_SHORT (launch.rs:411) and DEPOSIT_SHORT (mod.rs:558) reach the screens as core's English. Staking, a public launch and a public mix don't go through short.ts. Chunk 19 settled that Rust's messages stay English. STAKE_SHORT still says 'the Cardano account', the name short.ts's header (PY-10) dropped from the screens. That is wording only.
wasm merged_class (lib.rs:2166) doesn't canonicalise the legacy 'public' part as TS merged does (histories.ts:101). It can't be reached: the worker sends only canonical ids (readClass).

Outside the chunk, for whoever owns seedelf-data: whether the data layer's copies read tag-102 box datums and register datums as the wallet will after r3a#1 and x3#1 (the depth walk, the datum decoder, the crowd count). Also whether its contract index lists rows at the contract's old staked base address, as Koios's credential query does (address.rs:69-72 relies on that for CLI-era UTxOs).
